page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on x86_64 architecture running under the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 12 physical cores using hyperthreading on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU configuration includes 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and instruction set support for AVX-512 VNNI, AES cryptography, and FMA. System memory is provisioned at 48.0 GB, establishing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs, relying on remote block storage and featuring an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average multi-threaded performance, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 21007.3 and Geekbench multi-core reaching 8967.0. Single-core processing shows weaker relative throughput, recorded at 1313.3 on stress-ng single-core tests and 22.86 GB/sec on single-threaded gzip compression. Uncached memory write bandwidth reaches 47.99 GB/sec alongside an uncached read bandwidth of 108.94 GB/sec. Web serving throughput registers at 15.86 GB/sec, while Redis SET performance scales to 20.09 million operations per second. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high vCPU-to-RAM density provides compute-heavy parallel workloads with solid resource utilization per instance, though workloads bottlenecked by single-thread latency or requiring local storage disks will face architectural tradeoffs. Recommended workload fits include multi-threaded batch processing, distributed software compilation, media encoding, static web serving, and containerized backend microservices.
